Everything is possible.
A 21st Century Grammar School
"The school is determined that pupils experience ‘the exceptional every day’, and they do."Ofsted 2023 Learn more about the school
Academic Success
We know education is for life. Both inside and outside of the classroom we want our students to do exceptional things as an everyday occurrence and this enables them to achieve life changing qualifications. Our progress levels at GCSE are consistently among the very highest in Gloucestershire and make us the highest performing state girls' school in the South West. Our performance at GCSE and A Level combined has the Sunday Times Parent Power ranking us year on year as one of the top performing schools in the South West and within the top fifty state schools in the country.

Admissions
Each year we welcome 150 students into Year 7 from over 90 different primary schools. If you are thinking about applying to the school and wish to find out more about the test, how to prepare for it and how we support students in receipt of Pupil Premium go to our admission section.
Sixth Form
Our Sixth Form is a vibrant and progressive community. Made up of students from Stroud High School and 20 other schools it is an environment where young people can grow personally and flourish academically. Our students develop the love of their subjects in our full range of A-Level subjects whilst growing from our extensive range of personal development activities. Our students go on to attend the full range of Universities in the UK and abroad, Art colleges, higher apprenticeships, and scholarships.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
"Pupils thrive at this exceptional school." Ofsted 2023
Welcome to Stroud High School.
As a community we are on an exciting journey trying to define the 21st Century grammar school.
We want to be a school where bright students can thrive and flourish in an environment and culture which enables the “exceptional” to become an everyday occurrence. Our students and staff know that this takes hard work, the humility to keep improving and a passion for learning itself.
Our community is built on excellent relationships, a respect for individuality, a commitment to inclusivity as well as a sense of fun – the way we all treat each other is as important as what we do.
If we get this right then students will gain life changing qualifications ready for the next stage of their education, but more importantly equipped with the skills and character to take on the challenges of an ever-changing world. And they do. Our progress levels at GCSE are consistently among the very highest in Gloucestershire and make us the highest performing state girls' school in the South West. Our performance at GCSE and A Level combined has the Sunday Times Parent Power ranking us year on year as one of the top performing schools in the South West and within the top fifty state schools in the country. Year on year our students access the full range of Universities in the UK and abroad as well Art Colleges, Performing Arts Colleges and Higher Apprenticeships
We are proud of our community and are always willing to welcome visitors. Whether you are a prospective student, parent or a former student, you would be most welcome. Details about our Open Events can be found here or alternatively contact admissions@stroudhigh.gloucs.sch.uk to organise a private tour.

Our Values
"The school is determined that pupils experience ‘the exceptional every day’, and they do." Ofsted 2023
We believe that education is for life. It helps us to make sense of the world, our place within it and how we can contribute to it. But it’s also about making a difference. A brilliant education bestows knowledge that brings opportunity and with it comes responsibility. We teach our students to be the best they can by providing them with the skills, support and confidence to go out into the world and help make it a better place.
Our curriculum is broad and vibrant. Our community is dynamic and forward thinking. Both are built on our values of respect, courtesy, honour and a desire to help others. We encourage difference and embrace diversity. And we never forget the importance of fun, enjoyment and inclusivity in all that we do.
We don’t have a one size fits all approach or predetermined path. No matter what a young person wants to do we will prepare them to seize the world of opportunity that awaits. Most of all we are a community of like-minded students, teachers and parents. We are a mix of many different personalities, but are all on the same journey of discovery and united by the belief that we can make a positive difference to the world around us.
We believe in the strength of the human spirit, the brilliance of the human mind and, above all, that everything is possible.

About Us
Welcome to SHSF
"The school is determined that pupils experience ‘the exceptional every day’, and they do." Ofsted 2023
We welcome boys and girls from over 30 different schools from across the county and beyond. We don’t have a one size fits all approach – whatever your ambitions, we will help you get there.
When you join Stroud, you join a community of like-minded students, teachers and parents. No matter what you want to do – whether it’s going to university or starting your career – we’ll help you to get out there and seize the world of opportunity that awaits. We teach our students to be the best they can by providing them with the skills, support and confidence to go out into the world and make it a better place.
SHSF Values →← Wellbeing
Ofsted 2023
Stroud High School was inspected by Ofsted in November and was delighted to achieve ‘Outstanding’ across all of the five main elements of the inspection – Quality of education, Behaviour and attitudes, Personal development, Leadership and management and Sixth Form provision.
The inspectors had much to praise about the school, but notably the “...the highly ambitious vision” the school has for its pupils, the high standards of teaching, the “exemplary conduct” of the student body, and the mutual support given to and by all elements of the school. Inspectors wrote “Pupils thrive at this exceptional school. They relish their learning and the extensive opportunities for personal development.”
Since our last inspection in 2010, the school has expanded in size, and the curriculum and provision for the Sixth Form have significantly changed. Staff have worked so hard to transform our Sixth Form offer, and it was rightly graded as Outstanding in its own right. Inspectors wrote ”In the sixth form, study programmes are tailored carefully to students’ needs. The school has planned the curriculum with precision... As a result, they achieve exceptionally well. Sixth form students are prepared exceptionally well for their future destinations.”
The school was also acknowledged for its work to ensure that students with special educational needs and/or disabilities achieve as well as their peers, and that all students have support and opportunity to reach their full potential regardless of personal circumstances and background.

"Pupils consistently build new learning on secure foundations. As a result, they achieve exceptionally well." Ofsted 2023
We believe the environment at Stroud High helps our students to achieve and that our ethos of Everything is Possible has played a central role in helping us to become one of the UK's highest performing sixth forms.

Results
We believe the environment at Stroud High helps our students to achieve and that our ethos of Everything is Possible has played a central role in helping us to become one of the UK's highest performing sixth forms.
When we ask our students why they join us, over 90% of them say it is the quality of teaching and the learning environment.
Year on year our students achieve results that place Stroud High School amongst the very highest performing state schools in the South West, and within the top state schools in the country.
High quality examination performance has been sustained over a number of years. Every year, approximately three quarters of A Levels are graded from A*-B, and routinely around half of all grades are at A*/A.
2026 A Level Results
In 2026, our students achieve a 100% pass rate at A Level, with nearly half of all grades at A* or A. Of whom, 44% achieved a set of grades equivalent to AAB or above.

Partnerships
We are proud to work with many schools, organisations, businesses and groups.
International Partnerships
As a school we have 3 Modern Foreign Language partnerships with exchanges to schools in France, Spain and Germany. Our Sixth Form hosts students from Renens High School in the Canton de Vaud, Switzerland, as well as students from Germany and Italy.
Prior to Brexit, we ran Comenius Projects coordinating 7 schools from across the European Union.
We have an exchange with Hanbit High School in Paju, South Korea.
Annual International Exchanges
International Hosting
International Projects
We have held the full International School Award, awarded by the British Council tri-annually, since 2010 and have since been recognised for the outstanding quality of our international work. To achieve this award, a school must evidence, across and beyond the curriculum:
Prior to Brexit, we ran Erasmus+ (previously known as Comenius) projects coordinating 7 schools from across the European Union, and look forward to re-joining the programme in 2027. Post-Brexit, we have achieved Turing Scheme funding in 3 successive rounds of applications that facilitated our links with South Korea and Thailand.

International Award
Stroud High School encourages all students to be outward-looking and to participate in the wider world, providing many opportunities for students to build networks across the globe. The Penny Kruger International Prize is awarded annually in Y13 to the individual whose commitment to these ideals and international participation has been outstanding during their time in the school.

Educational Partnerships
As an outstanding school we work hard to contribute more widely to education in our local area. We learn best with, and from, other schools.
We are part of the Grammar School Heads Association (GSHA) working on developing provision in the selective sector. We are committed to widening access to the school and support GSHA in doing this work with the Department for Education through an explicit Memorandum of Understanding.
We collaborate with 8 primary schools across the Stroud District. On Wednesday afternoons Stroud High School Teachers and trained Sixth Form volunteers deliver lessons in Maths, Science, Languages and Music. This programme culminates with a Festival of Learning hosted on site at Stroud High School.
We are part of three different Teaching School Alliances. We have developed programmes on transition from Primary to Secondary school with CETA, delivered training for non-specialist language teachers with the Sir Thomas Rich’s Teaching Alliance, and year on year we provide training and mentor support for the National Professional Qualifications in Senior Leadership and Headship with the Odessey Teaching Alliance in Cheltenham.
We help develop and train teachers through our partnership with GITEP. Each year we host trainees across different subject areas. We also lead the provision for the training of all Modern Foreign Language teachers on the GITEP scheme in Gloucestershire.
We regularly provide training and support for Gloucestershire Association of School Business Managers.
Working With Industry
We are proud to give our students opportunities to work with local and countywide companies and organisations
Computing and Cyber Security
As a Cyber First Gold Award school, we work with many different organisations through NCSC Cyber First. Our partner company is Sopra Steria. We also work with Cygenta on this project
Several companies provide ementoring - these include CACI and BAE Systems
STEM and Local Organisations
Students in Y10-13 undertake Gold, Silver and Bronze Crest awards supported by local engineering firms, GE and Tony Gee.
Students in Key Stage 3 undertake electrical engineering sessions with Renishaw.
Other Organisations
Armed Forces
Over the past two years we have been working with the Royal Navy CCF to develop a Cadet Unit at Stroud High School. The unit is now partly operational, and we hope to increase the number of cadets across the school
Duke of Edinburgh
We partner with the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme and have a DofE license. The school routinely has over 200 students completing awards each year

Careers & Futures
"The school evaluates its careers programme carefully and ensures that pupils have meaningful encounters with the world of work." Ofsted 2023
Careers education begins in Year 7, giving students an early and informed understanding of the wide range of pathways available to them, and the subjects that will support their ambitions. A comprehensive programme runs throughout every year group, delivered through PSHE, curriculum‑linked lessons, guest speakers and assemblies. Students explore self‑development, career options and career management, enabling them to make confident decisions about further and higher education, as well as alternative routes such as apprenticeships.
Work‑related learning is embedded across the school, with students taking part in both virtual and in‑person work experience to broaden their understanding of the workplace. By the end of Sixth Form, the majority progress to leading universities, while an increasing number secure highly competitive higher‑education apprenticeships with top employers.
Our Careers Learning Journey provides an overview of the activities and events available to students throughout their time at SHS. Please note that some activities may be subject to change.
All Careers provision is aligned with the Career Development Institute Framework and the Gatsby Benchmarks, ensuring students develop the essential skills required in the modern workplace - including communication, leadership, independent learning, problem‑solving, teamwork, planning, motivation and strong interpersonal skills.
The school works in partnership with SGS College and Careers Service and Gloucestershire careers hub to provide independent unbiased careers guidance across all year groups.
Pathways - How SHS supports future pathways and key contacts - CLICK HERE
SHSF Advice on post 18 pathways - CLICK HERE
Our lead careers person is Mrs June Fletcher you can contact her on admin@stroudhigh.gloucs.sch.uk or telephone the school 01453 764441.
Click below to see the SHS Careers Learning Journey.
All staff and student have access to our Careers sharepoint via their onedrive login - CLICK HERE
Our Careers Governor is Mr David Pickard.

careers education intent july 2026
Programme of activities - Year 8
In May, the students spend half a day with a careers advisor thinking about the kind of lifestyle they would like in the future, researching a job of interest and learning about the different types and levels of qualifications and training routes, for example study at university and apprenticeships. In preparation for this day, the year 8s complete an activity at home creating their own town to help them think about the different jobs that would be needed in their town and to consider the wide range of different careers that exist, and about what might interest them in the future.
Where possible, we arrange for employers to come into the school to work with the students. For example, previously, two female civil engineers from Tony Gee LLP came to Stroud High School during year 8 science lessons. The civil engineers explained about the work that they do and how to become a civil engineer. The students were then given the task of building a bridge using the materials and the instructions provided.
Towards the end of Year 8, the students spend one lesson learning about Labour Market Information (LMI), what it means, where they can find LMI information and why it is important. The students research a range of different career sectors and jobs within these sectors. This activity is led by a careers advisor.
Programme of activities - Year 9
To support the students leading up to their GCSE option choices, they take part in and have access to a variety of resources and activities.
In small groups during January, the students take part in a how to choose your options 30-minute session with the careers advisor, this is a good opportunity for the students to fully consider their options and to ask questions.
In January, all Year 9 students receive an options booklet which contains information about the subject options available to them to study at KS4, the topics covered, how the students will be assessed and the careers that can lead from each subject.
Options evening is held at the school in January for the students, parents and carers, this is a good opportunity to speak to subject teachers and to see the careers advisor.
At the discretion of the Head of Year 9, a small number of careers interview appointments are available with a careers advisor for those students who need further support with their options choices.
Programme of activities - Year 10
At the start of the year, the students are asked to find a work shadowing placement/s before the end of term 5 for up to one week during the holidays or inset days. This is a fantastic opportunity to find out more about a career/working environment and to gain experience in the work place. Information about how to find a placement with contacts for local companies and organisations within in the Stroud, Gloucestershire and Bristol area along with virtual work experience opportunities nationally and a work shadowing journal is available in the Year 10 careers folder.
In June, the year 10s take part in a careers day aimed to inspire and help them to explore different opportunities. The day includes preparing for and interviewing 15 professions from a broad range of different careers about their job and the pathways available into their careers. This activity is completed in a “speed networking” style format. The students spend time reviewing and reflecting on the work experience they have completed and share what they have learned with the class. The students learn about Post 18 options, in small groups, learn, research and present to the rest of the class their findings for one of the Post 18 options e.g. Apprenticeships, study abroad, GAP years etc.
Programme of activities - Year 11
As part of the Personal Development curriculum, the Year 11 students take part in a how to choose your A Levels options lesson in term 2, during the lesson the students discuss and learn about the factors they should consider when choosing their options and complete personal research using the tools and websites provided. Students are encouraged to consider a range of Post 16 options, including alternative qualifications, and there is the opportunity to take part in subject taster days.
In term 2, the students receive a 20 minute Information, advice and guidance (IAG) meeting with a senior member of staff to discuss their plans for year 12 and 13.
The students have the chance of a 30 minute guidance interview with a careers advisor during term 2. This is an opportunity to discuss personal plans and options, to help with choosing pathways, receive reliable and useful information and websites to complete further research. Letters are sent home early in November via email, and to the students via their school email address.
During Terms 2 and 3, a number of different professional guest speakers from universities, businesses and societies come to Stroud High School. These talks have been recorded and distributed online this year.
Programme of activities - Year 12 and 13
At the start of Year 12, students are asked to arrange a work experience placement for the last week of term 6. Information on how to find a placement with contacts for local companies and organisations within the Stroud, Gloucestershire and Bristol area along with virtual work experience opportunities nationally and a work shadowing journal is available in the year 12 careers folder.
In Term 3, all Year 12 students attend talks organised by the sixth form about post 18 opportunities. The talks include an introduction to universities and how to research courses, information about degree and higher apprenticeship opportunities and for those considering a gap year, advice on how to plan constructive, gap year opportunities.
Year 12 students considering applying to highly competitive universities such as Oxbridge and Russell Group universities, begin to meet regularly from term 3 onwards in preparation for the application process. The sixth form organises a visit to Oxford University as well as the annual Oxbridge Conference and the group has access to various booklets and guides with key information to help them through the application and selection process. Wherever possible, students are also given the opportunity to practice their interview skills with a subject specialist. Mock interviews are usually arranged with professionals and experts from outside of the school to make the mock interview experience as realistic as possible.
For students considering competitive courses such as medicine, dentistry and veterinary careers, we have two teacher-mentors dedicated to advising on and coordinating activities in support of applications. The advice and guidance given includes bringing in professionals to talk about the applications process, advising on work experience opportunities and introducing students to undergraduates currently studying their chosen subjects to obtain an insight into their intended course and profession.
In Term 6, Year 12 students are encouraged to attend University Open Days. All students receive information about the UCAS application process from the head of sixth form begin to start the process. Those students who are not considering university are provided with information on Post-18 apprenticeships and attend a workshop with a careers advisor to help them consider their options. Information, useful websites and an action plan template is provided to help.
Year 12 and 13 students are offered a 45 minute guidance interview with a careers advisor during term 4. This is an opportunity to discuss personal plans and options, receive reliable and useful information and websites to complete further research. Letters are sent home early in February via email and to the students via their school email address. Careers meetings can be arranged at other times of the year where students need support.
A Next Steps evening is held in June for parents and carers of students in year 12 (students receive this information during tutor period). This information evening is delivered by the Head of Sixth Form, Head of Year 13 and the careers advisor and explains the options and opportunities available after year 13 along with information about the UCAS process, student finance and apprenticeship opportunities.
In year 13, students continue to receive support from the sixth form team preparing their UCAS application and preparing for interviews at both university and with apprenticeships.
Students are made aware of opportunities, vacancies and events throughout year 12 and 13, including summer school, work experience, careers events and apprenticeships. As well as the Careers and Futures page useful websites and links, there is also a Next Steps section on the school website with additional resources.
Students can also attend talks from a range of professionals, these talks have been recorded and distributed online this year.

Fantastic A Level Results for a Truly Special Year Group
13 August 2026
Students at Stroud High School are celebrating a stunning set of A Level results, with 17% of grades awarded at A*, 49% at A*-A, 78% at A*-B, and 44% of students achieving AAB or better.
But, as ever, the results only tell part of the story.
This has been a truly special year group. Alongside achieving outstanding academic outcomes, they have embraced every aspect of school life. They completed Gold Duke of Edinburgh awards in record numbers, lit up the stage in this year's production of Come From Away, raised more than £13,000 for Stroud Women's Refuge through RAG Week, performed in music concerts in Liverpool and Bruges, presented at education conferences in South Korea, competed in regional debating and national translation competitions in modern foreign languages, completed Gold CREST environmental projects, supported over 100 primary school lessons through the year, excelled in STEM olympiads, and helped lead the rich programme of house events that sits at the heart of the school community.
Headteacher Mark McShane said:
"I'm absolutely thrilled for the students who received their results this morning. They have worked so hard, but what makes this year group so memorable goes far beyond the grades they achieved.
They have excelled across all areas of curriculum and completed their qualifications to the highest standards, whilst somehow finding the time and energy to throw themselves into everything else that makes school life special. Quite remarkable.
More importantly, they have defined what it means to be a student at Stroud High School. They are kind, ambitious, inclusive and relentlessly positive young people and I have no doubt they have made our school a better place simply by being part of it.
They are genuinely a super-special year group, and we will miss them enormously.
I'd also like to pay tribute to the entire staff team at Stroud High School. These outcomes are the result of a huge collective effort. Year after year, our staff show what is possible when relationships sit at the heart of a school community. The care, encouragement, expertise and belief they invest in young people every day never ceases to amaze me. They are a fabulous team.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Smiles, Tears & Top Grades: Stroud High Students Celebrate GCSE Success | Stroud High School
pageCache.text:
Smiles, Tears & Top Grades: Stroud High Students Celebrate GCSE Success
20 August 2026
Students, staff and families at Stroud High School were celebrating this morning as Year 11 students collected an impressive set of GCSE results. This year, 22% of all grades awarded were Grade 9, the highest grade available at GCSE. More than half of all grades (51%) were awarded at Grades 9-8, while almost three-quarters (74%) were awarded at Grades 9-7.
The school was also particularly pleased by the number of students achieving consistently high grades across a broad range of subjects:
Mark McShane, Headteacher, said:
"Results day is always one of the highlights of the school year. The Sports Hall was full of smiles, hugs, happy tears and plenty of relieved students and parents, and it was a real privilege to share those moments with them."
"We must never underestimate that these results reflect years of hard work. It is no mean feat to perform so highly across the full range of GCSE subjects. The headline figures are excellent, but what matters most are the stories behind them. Every student has their own journey, and today we celebrate those who have exceeded expectations, reached personal goals and overcome challenges along the way."
"I'd also like to thank our staff and our parents and carers for the support, encouragement and care they have given throughout the last five years. Today's successes are the result of a genuine partnership. Above all, though, this day belongs to our students. They are quite rightly the stars of the show, and we couldn't be prouder of everything they have achieved."
Kim Pullon, Year Leader, said:
"I've had the privilege of working with this year group throughout their entire journey at Stroud High School, and I couldn't be prouder of them. Every student has their own story, and today has been full of moments where years of hard work, determination and resilience have paid off."
"The results are fantastic, but what I'll remember most are the smiles, the relief and the excitement in the Sports Hall this morning. They are a wonderful group of young people, and it has been a joy to watch them grow in confidence over the last five years. I can't wait to see what they go on to achieve next."
The school is delighted that so many Year 11 students will be returning to continue their studies at Stroud High Sixth Form in September. For all members of the year group, whatever their next step may be, Stroud High School wishes them every success and happiness for the future.

Academic Pathways
We recognise that all our students have different academic interests which is why at SHSF you can choose your own programme of study from our suite of 26 A Level subjects and 3 Additional Qualifications. You will work alongside specialists in your chosen subjects who will guide and mentor you on your sixth form journey.
Based on university guidance, the majority of our students follow a programme of 3 A Level subjects and an Additional Qualification with a small number opting to take Further Maths as a fourth A Level.
If you wish to undertake four A Levels, it is highly recommended that you have a GCSE profile of a minimum of 64 points from your best 8 GCSE grades. This advice is based on our knowledge of student experiences and academic outcomes.
It is generally advisable to choose the subjects that interest you the most, and that you most enjoy working on – an opportunity to pursue your passions and interests!
Scholarship and Learning Behaviours
At SHSF you will find an exceptional learning environment with challenging lessons centred on the development of independent learning. As part of your induction into academic A Level studies, we will introduce you to the philosophy of SHSF Learning Behaviours to help you achieve academic success and will equip you with the tools to support your scholarship work, the ability to think deeply and to be intellectually confident in your chosen subject disciplines. Each subject department will guide you as to what sort of scholarship work you can do in their subject area and will encourage you to create links between your reading and the curriculum, as well as regularly engaging with it through various different mediums, ranging from podcasts, online forums, articles and lectures to help grow your academic capability and potential. ​
To further support you in your A Level studies, we have dedicated Sixth Form study rooms with members of the Sixth Form Team on hand to provide advice and guidance.

We believe that all students should work towards their individual ambitions in school and beyond education. This applies to all students in the school, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
Our SEND team consists of the SENDCO - Mrs Nadine Moore, 2 student support mangers and 1 teaching assistant. However, all staff at Stroud High School work together to provide the best experience for students. All teachers are teachers of SEND.
We provide an inclusive curriculum, with the majority of our support provided by the individual teachers within the classroom.
All SEND students' needs are assessed on an individual basis and SEND Support Plans are put in place at an appropriate level following the graduated pathway. The House System
"Pupils are highly active citizens. They make significant contributions to the school and the local community." Ofsted 2023
On arriving at Stroud High School, each student is placed in a tutor group - 7A, 7C, 7G, 7K or 7S. Each tutor group forms part of a student-led House.
The Houses are named after mills in Stroud that were in production of goods in the 1600s-1800s representing the industrial heritage of the area:
Arundel - a fulling mill, purifying cloth
Capel - made woollen flock
Griffin - made cloth
Kimmin - milled flour
Stanley - made woollen cloth
The Student Leadership Team includes a Student Leader for each house.
House Leaders organise their houses to participate in the various activities and events throughout the year to try and gain as many house points as possible with the hope of being the overall winner at the end of the summer term.

Digital Strategy - Device Per Student
Our Digital Strategy
Stroud High School aims to become a 21st-century grammar school where exceptional learning is the norm. Central to this vision is the integration of digital technology in education, ensuring students thrive in a digitally-driven world.
We recognise technology and digital devices' integral and essential role in our everyday lives and workplaces. Education cannot remain unaffected by this, and we firmly believe that if we are to adequately prepare students for today’s world and continue to provide the highest levels of attainment then we need to provide an educational experience that embeds technology at the heart of it.
Over the next few years, we will be moving to a device-per-student provision for all year groups. A device-per-student provision means that each student will be equipped with a 2-in-1 touch screen device that they will use to access and complete their school work.
The transition to a device per student provision began in September 2024, with Year 12 moving to Bring Your Own Device Provision. In September 2025 Year 8 will move to school managed device per student provision.
